messages:
Maya Chen: Heads-up — planning kickoff for Q4 Dedicated capacity work. Need to lock on policies for surge handling, SLOs, and what we call 'grace lanes' vs full-isolation. Who's in for a quick sync tomorrow?
Samir Patel: +1. Important to include cost guardrails and what we auto-fall back to when dedicated pools hit limits.
Liam O'Neill: Can we sketch a matrix: trigger -> action -> customer-visible effect? short, concrete. e.g. cpu/gpu saturation at 85% for 2m -> enable limited burst (best-effort) -> notify + degraded latency.
Anita Gomez: We have two enterprise asks: 1) FinSecure wants guaranteed p99 < 120ms for their reserved lane, 2) MedFlow wants a guaranteed isolation lane that never gets preempted. Both are willing to pay for strict isolation.
Maya Chen: Good context. We need clear launch criteria: SLA definition, test harness, rollout plan, and cancellation/rollback rules. Draft idea: SLA tier names (standard, premium, isolated).
Samir Patel: Important: define eviction semantics for mixed-tenant GPUs. Proposal: soft-eviction (migrate to burst queue + burst credits) vs hard-eviction (terminate). Prefer soft first.
Liam O'Neill: +1 soft first. Also propose "surge containment zones" — small reserved pockets we only dip into when cluster-level demand spikes beyond normal autoscale window. Minimizes cross-customer tail latency.
Anita Gomez: For sales conversations, we need an explicit cost delta table. e.g. isolated lane = baseline + X% commit. Can we get a ballpark?
Samir Patel: I put a rough calc in the doc, but needs finance check. Quick pseudocode for the rule engine I shared in our working doc:
```
if pool_util > 0.85 for 120s:
  if customer_has_isolation: route -> isolated_nodes
  elif customer_burst_credits > 0: allow_burst(customer_id)
  else: queue_with_backoff(customer_id)
```
Maya Chen: Nice. For rollout: start with a canary (5% traffic) for premium customers, monitor p95/p99 latency and token cost delta, then expand. Need QA scenarios (cold-start, KV cache warm, large seq).
Liam O'Neill: Also add chaos tests for node preemption and simulated network partition. Make sure fallbacks don't create cascading retries.
Anita Gomez: Customer ask: SLA penalties? FinSecure wants financial credit if p99 > 120ms more than 3 days/month. Legal needs the exact wording. We should surface to sales: this is a heavy commitment.
Samir Patel: Suggest offering a service-level credit with caps and opt-in. Also include an escape hatch: automatic migration to dedicated hardware (higher cost) if repeated breaches.
Maya Chen: Agree. Can someone take the playbook draft + rollout checklist? I'll author the launch criteria.
Liam O'Neill: I'll take the operational runbook and chaos scenarios.
Anita Gomez: I'll draft the customer-facing cost & commitment language and sync with sales/legal.
Samir Patel: I'll formalize the rule engine and add telemetry signals we need (per-customer util, burst-credit balance, queue length).
roadmap-bot: Reminder: Roadmap sync meeting scheduled: Q4 Dedicated Capacity Work — Mon 09:00 PT. See calendar link :calendar:.
Maya Chen: Thanks — let's aim to have PRDs by EOD Friday so Eng can triage next week. Quick questions after — who owns SLA test harness infra?
Liam O'Neill: Ops team can prototype. I'll coordinate with eng-infra to spin up ephemeral clusters.
Anita Gomez: tagging @sales for heads-up after we finalize numbers.
Maya Chen: Great. If nobody objects, we'll proceed with the above scope: tiered SLAs, soft-eviction + burst credits, surge containment zones, canary rollout, customer opt-in for strict isolation. :thumbsup:
Samir Patel: No objections from me. :eyes:
Liam O'Neill: Sounds good.
Anita Gomez: Good to go from customer side.
Maya Chen: Ok closing thread — will post the PRD link shortly.
